'''Seigo Tarucha''' (born 1953) is a Japanese experimental physicist who is known for his research on gate-defined [[semiconductor]] [[quantum dot]]s and [[spin qubit]]s.

== Biography ==
Tarucha was born 1953 in [[Ehime Prefecture]].<ref>author biographies in: {{cite journal |first1=Akira |last1=Oiwa |first2=Takafumi |last2=Fujita |first3=Haruki |last3=Kiyama |first4=Giles |last4=Allison |first5=Arne |last5=Ludwig |first6=Andreas D. |last6=Wieck and |first7=Seigo |last7=Tarucha |title=Conversion from Single Photon to Single Electron Spin Using Electrically Controllable Quantum Dots |journal=J. Phys. Soc. Jpn. |volume=86 |article-number=011008 |date=2017 |doi=10.7566/JPSJ.86.011008}}</ref> He studied ''Applied Physics'' at the [[University of Tokyo]], where he obtained his BS in 1976, his MSc in 1978, and his PhD in 1986.<ref name="baqis"/><ref>{{cite web |url=https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/author/38356897600 |title=Seigo Tarucha |work=ieee.org |date=2008-09-26 |access-date=2024-05-21}}</ref> In 1978 he joined [[Nippon Telegraph and Telephone#R&D laboratories|NTT Basic Research Laboratories]] as ''Staff Member'', becoming ''Senior Researcher'' (1985), ''Principal Researcher'' (1989), ''Group Leader'' (1990), and ''Distinguished Scientist'' (1994–1998) there.<ref name="riken">{{cite journal |url=https://cems.riken.jp/wp-content/themes/riken/material/pdf/cems-catalog-en.pdf |title=Quantum Functional System Research Group |journal=CEMS |publisher=RIKEN |date=2023 |page=31 |access-date=2025-01-14}}</ref><ref name="baqis">{{cite journal |url=http://en.baqis.ac.cn/upload/file/20211129/e26b6c63ff404cf98b5464676fd030ed.pdf |title=About the speakers: Seigo Tarucha |journal=3rd International Symposium on Quantum Physics and Quantum Information Sciences (QPQIS2021) |publisher=Beijing Academy of Quantum Information Sciences |date=2021 |format=pdf |page=18 |access-date=2025-01-14}}</ref> In 1998 he was appointed professor at the Department of Physics at the University of Tokyo and from 2004 to 2018 he was professor in the Department of Applied Physics at the same university. In 2013, he joined [[RIKEN]], where he was named ''Division Director'' of the Quantum Information Electronics Division and ''Group Director'' of the Quantum Functional System Research Group, both at the RIKEN Center for Emergent Matter Science. Since 2018 he is also ''Deputy Director'' of this center and he also heads the ''Semiconductor Quantum Information Device Research Team'' (since 2020) and the ''Emergent Phenomena Observation Technology Research Team'' (since 2024).<ref name="riken"/><ref>{{cite web |url=https://cems.riken.jp/en/laboratory/qfsrg |title=Homepage including brief CV |work=riken.jp |access-date=2024-05-21}}</ref>

In his research, Tarucha has studied the quantum physics of [[GaAs]] and [[silicon]] nanostructures, in particular the transport through [[quantum dot]]s and quantum dot molecules (including investigations of the [[Kondo effect]] with quantum dots) and their spin physics. His research contributed to establishing the basic control and measurement operations for these systems (controlled charging of the dots, single-shot spin measurement, microwave [[spectroscopy]], coherent control using [[Electron paramagnetic resonance|ESR]] and time-dependent gate voltages to modify the [[Exchange interaction|exchange coupling]] between neighboring quantum dots) and demonstrating the quantum dots atom- and molecule-like properties.<ref>{{cite journal |title=Shell filling and spin effects in a few electron quantum dot |last1=Tarucha |first1=S |last2=Austing |first2=D G |last3=Honda |first3=T |last4=van der Hage |first4=R J |last5=Kouwenhoven |first5=L P |journal=Phys. Rev. Lett. |volume=77 |issue=17 |pages=3613-3616 |date=1996 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.77.3613}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |title=Microwave spectroscopy of a quantum-dot molecule |last1=Oosterkamp |first1=TH |last2=Fujisawa |first2=T |last3=van der Wiel |first3=W G |last4=Ishibashi |first4=K |last5=Hijman |first5=R V |last6=Tarucha |first6=S |last7=Kouwenhoven |first7=L P |volume=395 |issue=6705 |pages=873-876 |journal=Nature |date=1998 |doi=10.1038/27617|arxiv=cond-mat/9809142 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |title=Allowed and forbidden transitions in artificial hydrogen and helium atoms |last1=Fujisawa |first1=T |last2=Austing |first2=DG |last3=Tokura |first3=Y |last4=Hirayama |first4=Y |last5=Tarucha |first5=S |journal=Nature |volume=419 |issue=6904 |pages=278-281 |date=2002 |doi=10.1038/nature00976|arxiv=cond-mat/0209464 }}</ref> Much of his work since the late 1990s addressed the potential use of electron spins in quantum dots as [[qubit]]s for [[quantum information processing]] following the [[Spin qubit quantum computer|Loss-DiVincenzo proposal]]. Work in his group demonstrated among others electrically-driven single-<ref>{{cite journal |title=Electrically driven single-electron spin resonance in a slanting Zeeman field |last1=Pioro-Ladrière |first1=M |last2=Obata |first2=T |last3=Tokura |first3=Y |last4=Shin |first4=YS |last5=Kubo |first5=T |last6=Yoshida |first6=K |last7=Taniyama |first7=T |last8=Tarucha |first48=S |journal=Nature Physics |volume=4 |issue=10 |page=776-779 |doi=10.1038/nphys1053|arxiv=0805.1083 }}</ref> and two-qubit [[quantum gate]]s.<ref>{{cite journal |title=Two-Qubit Gate of Combined Single-Spin Rotation and Interdot Spin Exchange in a Double Quantum Dot |last1=Brunner |first1=R |last2=Shin |first2=YS |last3=Obata |first3=T |last4=Pioro-Ladrière |first4=M |last5=Kubo |first5=T |last6=Yoshida |first6=K |last7=Taniyama |first7=T |last8=Tokura |first8=Y |last9=Tarucha |first9=S |journal=Phys. Rev. Lett. |volume=107 |issue=14 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.107.146801|arxiv=1109.3342 }}</ref> More recently, his group demonstrated a quantum-dot spin qubit with a [[fidelity]] above 99.9% in 2018<ref>{{cite journal |first1=J. |last1=Yoneda |first2=K. |last2=Takeda |first3=T. |last3=Otsuka |first4=T. |last4=Nakajima |first5=M. R. |last5=Delbecq |first6=G. |last6=Allison |first7=T. |last7=Honda |first8=T. |last8=Kodera |first9=S. |last9=Oda |first10=Y. |last10=Hoshi |first11=N. |last11=Usami |first12=K. M. |last12=Itoh |first13=S. |last13=Tarucha |title=A quantum-dot spin qubit with coherence limited by charge noise and fidelity higher than 99.9% |journal=Nature Nanotech. |volume=13 |pages=102-106 |date=2018 |arxiv=1708.01454 |doi=10.1038/s41565-017-0014-x}}</ref> and [[quantum error correction]] using a three-qubit code.<ref>{{cite journal |title=Quantum error correction with silicon spin qubits |first1=Kenta |last1=Takeda |first2=Akito |last2=Noiri |first3=Takashi |last3=Nakajima |first4=Takashi |last4=Kobayashi |first5=Seigo |last5=Tarucha |journal=Nature |volume=608 |pages=682-686 |date=2022 |doi=10.1038/s41586-022-04986-6 |arxiv=2201.08581}}</ref>

According to [[Web of Science]] he has (as of 2024) co-authored over 500 research articles in peer-reviewed journals which were cited more than 24,000 times ([[h-index]] of 66).<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.webofscience.com/wos/woscc/citation-report/e5d86cd6-9a3b-4cba-b1ba-b154d4395b7d-e814d9ac |title=Citation Report: SEIGO TARUCHA |work=webofscience.com |access-date=2024-05-21}}</ref> Among others, he is co-author of several highly cited review articles on the physics of few-electron gate-defined quantum dots.<ref>{{cite journal |title=Spins in few-electron quantum dots |last1=Hanson |first1=R |last2=Kouwenhoven |first2=L. P. |last3=Petta |first3=J. R. |last4=Tarucha |first4=S. |last5=Vandersypen |first5=L. M. K. |journal=Rev. Mod. Phys. |volume=79 |issue=4 |pages=1217-1265 |date=2007 |doi=10.1103/RevModPhys.79.1217|arxiv=cond-mat/0610433 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |title=Electron transport through double quantum dots |last1=van der Wiel |first1=W. G. |last2=De Franceschi |first2=S. |last3=Elzerman |first3=J. M. |last4=Fujisawa |first4=T. |last5=Tarucha |first5=S. |last6=Kouwenhoven |first6=L. P. |journal=Rev. Mod. Phys. |volume=75 |issue=1 |pages=1-22 |date=2003 |doi=10.1103/RevModPhys.75.1|arxiv=cond-mat/0205350 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |title=Few-electron quantum dots |last1=Kouwenhoven |first1=L. P. |last2=Austing |first2=D. G. |last3=Tarucha |first3=S. |journal=Rep. Prog. Phys. |volume=64 |issue=6 |pages=701-736 |date=2001 |doi=10.1088/0034-4885/64/6/201}}</ref>

== Awards ==
* 2000 Ryogo Kubo Award<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nii.ac.jp/qis/first-quantum/e/subgroups/spinQcom/researcher.html |title=Spin Quantum Computers: Subtopic Leader Seigo Tarucha |work=nii.ac.jp |date= |access-date=2025-01-14}}</ref>
* 2002 [[Nishina Memorial Prize]]<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nishina-mf.or.jp/project_en/kinen_en/ |title=Nishina Memorial Prize |work=nishina-mf.or.jp |language=en |access-date=2024-05-21}}</ref>
* 2005 [[Medals of Honor (Japan)#Purple ribbon|National Medal with Purple Ribbon]]<ref>{{cite web |title=各賞受賞一覧 |url=https://www.u-tokyo.ac.jp/ja/research/systems-data/d01_01.html |website=東京大学 |access-date=3 September 2025 |language=ja}}</ref>
* 2007 [[Leo Esaki]] Prize<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.i-step.org/prize/esaki/laureates_en.html |title=Past Leo Esaki Prize winners |language=en |access-date=2024-05-21 |quote=for the realization of artificial atoms and molecules and the challenge of quantum computing}}</ref>
* 2017 ''Outstanding Achievement Award'' of the [[Japan Society of Applied Physics]]<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.jsap.or.jp/english/awards/outstanding-achievement-award/recipients |title=JSAP Outstanding Achievement Award Recipients |work=jsap.or.jp |language=en |access-date=2024-05-21}}</ref>
